statements.statement: If \(z_0\) is a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\), then for every real shift \(d\), \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), this gives \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0\) and \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\); whenever this value is nonzero, \(\theta_0=E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]/E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\).
statements.justification: This exact identity displays the global location-family null score and its relevance under residual contamination.
statements.gap: Transform-zero incompleteness is classical, but its multiplicity-adjusted score has not been used to eliminate an arbitrary PLM covariate shift created by a supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: Known-noise implementations can estimate the causal coefficient by a single bounded or exponentially weighted moment ratio.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(z_0\) be a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\).  Thus
\[
M^{(j)}(z_0)=0\quad(0\le j<\ell),
\qquad
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0.
\]
All differentiations below are legitimate.  Indeed, on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), sub-Gaussianity of \(\eta\), boundedness of \(D_n\), and conditional sub-Gaussianity of \(\xi\) give every polynomial--exponential moment used below; dominated convergence therefore permits differentiation under the expectation.  Equivalently, for the first identity one may use directly that \(M\) is the displayed entire moment generating function.

Fix \(d\in\mathbb R\) and define \(L_d(z)=E_P[e^{z(\eta+d)}]\).  Since \(d\) is deterministic,
\[
L_d(z)=e^{zd}M(z).
\]
By the derivative representation of an entire moment generating function and the Leibniz rule,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]
&=E_P[(\eta+d)^{\ell-1}e^{z_0(\eta+d)}]\\
&=L_d^{(\ell-1)}(z_0)\\
&=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
  {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality is precisely the multiplicity condition.  It also covers the boundary case \(\ell=1\), when the sum consists only of \(M(z_0)=0\).

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By the clipped range of \(\bar g_n\) and the class condition \(\lVert g_0\rVert_\infty\le C_g\),
\[
|D_n|=|g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)|\le2C_g
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
In particular, all following conditional expectations exist.  The variable \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), and \(\eta\perp X\) by the independent-treatment-noise assumption.  Applying the deterministic-shift identity conditionally with \(d=D_n\) gives
\[
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]
=E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+D_n)\mid X]
=0
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]

For relevance, independence of \(\eta\) and \(D_n\) yields, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]
=M(z)H_n(z).
\]
Because \(Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)=Z_n^\ell e^{z_0Z_n}\), differentiation and then the Leibniz rule give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
&=F_n^{(\ell)}(z_0)\\
&=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}{\ell\choose j}
  M^{(j)}(z_0)H_n^{(\ell-j)}(z_0)\\
&=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every summand with \(j<\ell\) vanishes by multiplicity, and \(j=\ell\) is the only remaining summand.  Since \(M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\ne0\), the scalar relevance condition is equivalently \(H_n(z_0)\ne0\); no overlap or additional rank condition is used.

Finally, put \(b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n\).  The residual definitions give the structural decomposition
\[
Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi.
\]
The boundedness assumptions on \(q_0\), \(\theta_0\), and \(D_n\) ensure that \(b_n\) is bounded.  Hence the conditional annihilation just proved implies
\[
E_P[b_n(X)J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=E_P\!\left[b_n(X)E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]\right]
=0.
\]
Moreover, \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\).  The outcome-mean-independence assumption therefore gives
\[
E_P[\xi J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]
=0.
\]
Multiplying the structural decomposition by \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) and taking expectations now yields
\[
E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=\theta_0E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)].
\]
Whenever the displayed denominator is nonzero, division is valid and proves
\[
\theta_0
=\frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
        {E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]
Thus the moment ratio is an identifying functional for the causal coefficient under the stated structural assumptions and the explicit nonzero-relevance boundary condition; the equality is not imposed by definition.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)\) and \(G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statements.justification: The identity recovers the latent transform-zero geometry from observable learned residuals and isolates an analytic nuisance ratio.
statements.gap: Classical convolution results do not provide the outcome transform \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+MB_n\) for a partially linear causal coefficient.
statements.consumer: The contour theorem integrates \(G_n/F_n\) and removes \(B_n/H_n\) exactly.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(z\in\mathbb C\).  Since \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), the independence \(\eta\perp X\) gives
\[
 F_n(z)
 =E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)H_n(z).
\]
All transforms in this display are entire: \(D_n\) is bounded by the clipping and range restrictions, while the sub-Gaussian bound on \(\eta\) supplies an integrable exponential envelope on every compact subset of \(\mathbb C\).  The same envelope permits differentiation under the expectation, so
\[
 F_n'(z)=E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}].
\]
Using the identity \(Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_n(z)
 &=\theta_0E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}]
   +E_P[b_n(X)e^{zZ_n}]
   +E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]\\
 &=\theta_0F_n'(z)
   +E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}e^{z\eta}].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, \(e^{zZ_n}\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), and therefore the outcome mean-independence restriction gives
\[
 E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P\!\left[e^{zZ_n}E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]=0.
\]
Finally, \(b_n(X)e^{zD_n}\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), so a second use of \(\eta\perp X\) gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}e^{z\eta}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Combining the displays proves both identities for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).

statements.statement: Let \(C_j\) be positively oriented. If \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), then \(\theta_0=\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).
statements.justification: The observable contour formula identifies the coefficient without learning the outcome regression or separating the two transform factors.
statements.gap: Location-family completeness and real-zero tests do not construct this observable complex contour functional for a PLM coefficient.
statements.consumer: The adaptive estimator evaluates the identifying functional on a pilot-selected contour.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\), on the contour \(C_j\),
\[
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}
   +\frac{M(z)B_n(z)}{M(z)H_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}.
\]
The first equality is valid because \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\).  The quotient \(B_n/H_n\) is analytic on and inside \(C_j\), because both functions are entire and \(H_n\) is zero-free there.  Cauchy's integral theorem therefore gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}\,dz=0.
\]
The argument principle and the assumed boundary zero-freeness give
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\theta_0N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
The assumed positive zero count licenses division by \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\).  The resulting expression is exactly \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)\) from \(\text{def:contour-functional}\), proving the claim.

statements.statement: There is \(A_k<\infty\), depending only on \(k\), such that every centered law with \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), where \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\).
statements.justification: A uniform estimator requires usable spectral information in a disk fixed by primitive class constants.
statements.gap: Quantitative Marcinkiewicz results control Gaussian approximation from zero-free disks; this converse direction localizes a zero from fixed cumulant separation.
statements.consumer: The contour bank only searches the fixed disk determined here.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(c_{\psi}<\infty\) be the universal constant in the moment-generating-function consequence of the \(\psi_2\) bound:
\[
 E_P[e^{t\eta}]\le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}t^{2}),
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
This follows directly by expanding the exponential and using the sub-Gaussian moment bounds \(\|\eta\|_{L^p}\le C\psi_{\eta}\sqrt p\).  Hence, for complex \(z\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le E_P[e^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}]
 \le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}|z|^{2}).
\]

Fix \(R>0\) and suppose, toward a contradiction, that \(M\) has no zero in \(\{|z|\le R\}\).  Since the disk is simply connected and \(M(0)=1\), there is an analytic logarithm \(K=\log M\) on a neighborhood of the disk, normalized by \(K(0)=0\).  Put \(A=c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2}\).  The preceding display implies
\[
 \operatorname{Re}K(z)=\log|M(z)|\le A,
 \qquad |z|\le R.
\]
For completeness, the needed analytic bound follows without an additional probabilistic assumption.  The function
\[
 h(z)=\frac{K(z)}{2A-K(z)}
\]
satisfies \(|h(z)|\le1\), because
\[
 |2A-K(z)|^{2}-|K(z)|^{2}
 =4A\{A-\operatorname{Re}K(z)\}\ge0,
\]
and \(h(0)=0\).  Applying the Schwarz inequality after rescaling the radius-
\(R\) disk gives \(|h(z)|\le |z|/R\).  Thus, for \(|z|\le R/2\),
\[
 |K(z)|\le \frac{2A(|z|/R)}{1-|z|/R}\le2A.
\]
The Cauchy coefficient formula on \(|z|=R/2\) now yields
\[
 |\kappa_k(\eta)|=|K^{(k)}(0)|
 \le k!\frac{2A}{(R/2)^k}
 =2^{k+1}c_{\psi}k!\,\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2-k}.
\]
Choose
\[
 A_k=(2^{k+2}c_{\psi}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}.
\]
If \(M\) were zero-free on the radius-\(R_0\) disk, the preceding inequality would give \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\le\delta/2\), contradicting cumulant separation.  Therefore \(M\) has a zero with \(|z|\le R_0\).  This choice has the asserted dependence and, in particular, \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\), with equality for the displayed choice.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) yields finite \(J\), radii \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) with \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\). The conclusion is uniform in \(n\).
statements.justification: Pointwise zero existence does not imply uniform risk; compact-open closure and boundary stability must produce a finite conditioned bank.
statements.gap: Existing pointwise transform-zero theory and zero-free-disk inequalities do not establish a finite contour cover uniform over this cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian class.
statements.consumer: A finite bank makes selection measurable and reduces stochastic control to finitely many contour ratios.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr M\) be the locally uniform closure appearing in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\).  We first verify the compactness and closure facts needed by the finite-subcover argument.

The sub-Gaussian assumption gives a universal constant \(c_{\psi}<\infty\) such that every transform in the original family obeys
\[
 |M(z)|
 \le E[e^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}]
 \le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}|z|^{2}),
 \qquad z\in\mathbb C.
\]
Thus the family is uniformly bounded on every compact disk.  Cauchy's formula on a slightly larger disk makes it equicontinuous on the smaller disk.  Successive finite-net extraction on disks of integer radius, followed by a diagonal argument, gives a locally uniformly convergent subsequence from every sequence in the original family.

Every locally uniform limit is again the moment generating function of an admissible law.  Indeed, the corresponding laws have uniformly bounded second moments and hence are tight.  Along a weakly convergent subsequence, the common sub-Gaussian envelope makes \(e^{t\eta}\) uniformly integrable for each real \(t\).  Therefore the moment generating function of the weak limit agrees with the locally uniform analytic limit on the real axis, and the identity theorem extends the agreement to \(\mathbb C\).  Centering passes to the limit by uniform integrability.  The sub-Gaussian norm bound is weakly closed: for every \(u>\psi_{\eta}\), Portmanteau's inequality applied to \(x\mapsto e^{x^{2}/u^{2}}\), followed by \(u\downarrow\psi_{\eta}\), gives \(\|\eta_{\infty}\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).  Finally, locally uniform convergence implies convergence of every derivative at zero.  Since the \(k\)-th cumulant is a polynomial in the first \(k\) derivatives of an MGF whose value at zero is one,
\[
 |\kappa_k(M_{\infty})|
 =\lim_m|\kappa_k(M_m)|
 \ge\delta.
\]
The same conclusion applies to sequences in the closure by choosing, for their \(m\)-th terms, original-family approximants within \(m^{-1}\) on the disk of radius \(m\).  Since the compact-open topology on entire functions is metrizable, the preceding sequential compactness proves that \(\mathscr M\) is compact.  It also proves that every \(M\in\mathscr M\) satisfies the hypotheses of \(\text{lem:zero-localization}\), so every such \(M\) has a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\).

Suppose first that \(\mathscr M\neq\varnothing\), and fix \(M_{\circ}\in\mathscr M\).  Because \(M_{\circ}(0)=1\), it is not identically zero, and its zeros are isolated.  It therefore has only finitely many zeros in the compact annulus \(R_0\le |z|\le R_1\).  Choose
\[
 \rho(M_{\circ})\in(R_0,R_1)
\]
which is not the modulus of any of those zeros, and put \(C(M_{\circ})=\{z:|z|=\rho(M_{\circ})\}\).  This circle is zero-free, encloses the zero supplied by \(\text{lem:zero-localization}\), and satisfies
\[
 m(M_{\circ})
 :=\inf_{z\in C(M_{\circ})}|M_{\circ}(z)|>0,
 \qquad
 N_{C(M_{\circ})}(M_{\circ})\ge1.
\]
Define the compact-open neighborhood
\[
 \mathcal U(M_{\circ})
 =\left\{\widetilde M\in\mathscr M:
 \sup_{z\in C(M_{\circ})}
 |\widetilde M(z)-M_{\circ}(z)|<\frac{m(M_{\circ})}{2}
 \right\}.
\]
For \(\widetilde M\in\mathcal U(M_{\circ})\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
 \inf_{z\in C(M_{\circ})}|\widetilde M(z)|
 \ge\frac{m(M_{\circ})}{2}.
\]
Moreover, for \(t\in[0,1]\), the boundary function \(M_{\circ}+t(\widetilde M-M_{\circ})\) is nonzero.  Its argument-principle integral is continuous in \(t\) and integer-valued, hence constant.  Consequently
\[
 N_{C(M_{\circ})}(\widetilde M)
 =N_{C(M_{\circ})}(M_{\circ})
 \ge1.
\]

The neighborhoods \(\mathcal U(M_{\circ})\) cover the compact set \(\mathscr M\).  Choose a finite subcover centered at \(M_1,\ldots,M_J\), and set
\[
 \rho_j=\rho(M_j),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=\frac12\min_{1\le j\le J}m(M_j)>0,
 \qquad
 C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}.
\]
For every \(M\in\mathscr M\), membership in one selected neighborhood gives, for the corresponding \(j\),
\[
 N_{C_j}(M)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
Every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) belongs to the original family and hence to \(\mathscr M\), so the conclusion holds uniformly in \(n\).  If the original family is empty, take \(J=1\), any \(\rho_1\in(R_0,R_1)\), and any \(a_{\star}>0\); the conclusion is then vacuous.

Only \(k,\delta,\psi_{\eta},R_0,R_1\) enter this existence argument.  The finite subcover and its radii are nonconstructive.  Once any resulting tuple is fixed, it is deterministic and independent of \(n\), \(P\), and the sample, but no effective enumeration, numerical modulus, or algorithm for finding it has been proved.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.
statements.justification: The lower bound uses an explicit Gaussian-outcome-innovation path that preserves the law of \((X,T)\), both regression functions, and the deterministic supplied codes.
statements.gap: A generic appeal to a parametric submodel does not verify membership in a triangular common-code class.
statements.consumer: Le Cam's two-point lemma turns this construction into the \(c/n\) half of the spectral minimax rate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and suppose that \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\).  Choose \(P_{\star}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  Retain from \(P_{\star}\) the joint law of \((X,T)\), the covariate marginal, the functions \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), and hence \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\).  The supplied codes and their clipped versions \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) are deterministic experiment inputs and are retained as well.

Let
\[
 c_{\mathrm N}=\lVert N(0,1)\rVert_{\psi_2},
 \qquad
 \tau=\frac{\psi_{\xi}}{2c_{\mathrm N}}>0,
 \qquad
 c_0=\min\{C_{\theta},1\}>0.
\]
On a product extension, let \(\xi_{\star}\sim N(0,\tau^2)\) be independent of \((X,T)\).  For every \(\vartheta\in[-c_0,c_0]\), define
\[
 Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star},
\]
and let \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) be the resulting law of \((X,T,Y_{\vartheta})\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  The law of \((X,T)\) is unchanged, so \(g_0\), \(\eta\), the independence \(\eta\perp X\), the treatment sub-Gaussian bound, the order-\(k\) cumulant separation, the range bound on \(g_0\), and
\[
 \lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}
\]
are inherited from \(P_{\star}\).  Centering and independence of \(\eta\) give
\[
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta}}[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X]
 =q_0(X)+\vartheta E_{P_{\star}}[\eta\mid X]
 =q_0(X).
\]
Thus the outcome regression remains exactly \(q_0\), including \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\).  Conditional on \((X,T)\),
\[
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta}}[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X,T]
 =q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta,
 \qquad
 E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0.
\]
Hence the partially linear coefficient is \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\), and its outcome innovation is \(\xi_{\star}\).  This coefficient is unique: cumulant separation implies that \(\eta\) is not almost surely zero, so two distinct coefficients cannot give the same conditional mean.  The boundary condition holds because \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\le C_{\theta}\).  Finally, Gaussian scaling and independence yield
\[
 \lVert\xi_{\star}\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}
 =c_{\mathrm N}\tau
 =\frac{\psi_{\xi}}2
 \le\psi_{\xi}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Its variance \(\tau^2\) is strictly positive and depends only on the fixed class constant \(\psi_{\xi}\) and the universal norm convention.  Therefore \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\).  No outcome-code restriction is used.

It remains to calculate the divergence.  The laws \(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\) and \(P_{n,\vartheta_1}\) have the same \((X,T)\) marginal.  Given \((X,T)\), their outcome distributions are Gaussian with common variance \(\tau^2>0\) and means differing by \((\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)\eta\).  The conditional chain rule for relative entropy and the equal-variance Gaussian density calculation give
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}\right)
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}
 E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2].
\]
The defining exponential-moment inequality for the \(\psi_2\)-norm implies, for a universal \(c_2<\infty\),
\[
 E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2]\le c_2\psi_{\eta}^2.
\]
Additivity of relative entropy for product measures now shows that, whenever \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}
          \middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
 &=nD_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}
          \middle\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}\right)\\
 &=\frac{h^2}{2\tau^2}E_{P_{\star}}[\eta^2]\\
 &\le \frac{c_2\psi_{\eta}^2}{2\tau^2}h^2
 =:C_0h^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The constants \(c_0\) and \(C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.  The only boundary conditions used are \(C_{\theta}>0\), \(\psi_{\xi}>0\), and cumulant separation; no propensity overlap, inverse, or rank condition is involved.

statements.statement:
For \(n\ge2\), suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\). There are \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le\frac Cn.
\]
The estimator uses \(\bar g_n\), uses no supplied outcome code, and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
No inclusion of the broad class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is asserted; the finite-order ACE comparison is confined to the separately defined subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
statements.justification: Exact observable transform geometry yields a computable unknown-noise estimator with matched parametric MSE on the broad direct-L1 class.
statements.gap: Published finite-order ACE guarantees retain nuisance terms and do not give a uniform unknown-noise contour estimator on the broader no-outcome-code class.
statements.consumer: An analyst can attain parametric coefficient risk with a small fixed treatment-code error and no outcome learner under fixed spectral separation.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m_a=|I_a|\).  For \(n\ge2\), both half-samples are nonempty and \(m_a\ge n/3\).  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\).

By \(\text{lem:finite-contour-bank}\), there is an index \(j_{\star}=j_{\star}(P)\) such that
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(M)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{z\in C_{j_{\star}}}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
By \(\text{lem:l1-nuisance-zero-free}\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on the disk \(|z|\le R_1\), \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) there, and \(F_n=M H_n\) has the same zeros as \(M\), with multiplicity.  Consequently,
\[
 N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{z\in C_{j_{\star}}}|F_n(z)|\ge\frac{3a_{\star}}4. \tag{1}
\]

For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 d_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 e_a=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|,
\]
and define the regular events \(\mathcal A_a=\{d_a\le a_{\star}/8\}\).  On \(\mathcal A_0\), (1) gives
\[
 \inf_{C_{j_{\star}}}|\widehat F_{0,n}|
 \ge\frac{5a_{\star}}8.
\]
Rouch\'e's theorem applies because \(d_0\le a_{\star}/8<3a_{\star}/4\le\inf_{C_{j_{\star}}}|F_n|\).  Thus
\[
 \widehat N_{0j_{\star},n}=N_{C_{j_{\star}}}(F_n)\ge1,
\]
so \(j_{\star}\) is pilot-admissible.  The maximizing rule in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) therefore selects an index \(\widehat j_n\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{0,n}|
 \ge\frac{5a_{\star}}8,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|F_n|
 \ge\frac{a_{\star}}2. \tag{2}
\]
Another application of Rouch\'e's theorem, now using \(d_0\le a_{\star}/8<a_{\star}/2\), gives
\[
 \widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}=N_{C_{\widehat j_n}}(F_n)\ge1. \tag{3}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), (2) also yields
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{1,n}|
 \ge\frac{3a_{\star}}8>\frac{a_{\star}}4, \tag{4}
\]
so the evaluation fallback is not used.

The selector is measurable.  Indeed, under the fixed circle parameterization, each empirical transform and its derivative are jointly measurable in the sample and continuous in the circle parameter.  Hence each boundary infimum is the infimum over a fixed countable dense set of angles and is measurable.  On the measurable zero-free event, the winding integral is a measurable integral of a jointly measurable continuous integrand.  The bank is finite, and the smallest-index tie and failure rules are deterministic.  Thus \(\widehat j_n\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) are sample-measurable once the non-effective deterministic bank has been fixed.

There is a class-uniform constant \(C_G<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|G_n(z)|\le C_G. \tag{5}
\]
To see this, use \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), and Cauchy--Schwarz to obtain
\[
 |G_n(z)|
 \le E_P[|Y|e^{R_1|Z_n|}]
 \le e^{2C_gR_1}\lVert Y\rVert_{L^2(P)}
       \{E_P[e^{2R_1|\eta|}]\}^{1/2}.
\]
The range bounds, \(|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}\), and the two sub-Gaussian assumptions bound both factors uniformly, proving (5).

On \(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1\), let \(C=C_{\widehat j_n}\) and let the common positive integer in (3) be \(N\).  Since \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C\), \(\text{thm:exact-contour-identification}\) gives
\[
 \theta_0
 =\frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (2), (4), (5), \(N\ge1\), and the fact that the circle length is at most \(2\pi R_1\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|
 \frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_C
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz
 -\theta_0
 \right|\\
 &\quad\le R_1\left\{
 \frac{e_1}{3a_{\star}/8}
 +\frac{C_Gd_1}{(3a_{\star}/8)(a_{\star}/2)}
 \right}
 \le L_{\star}(d_1+e_1), \tag{7}
 \end{aligned}
\]
where \(L_{\star}<\infty\) depends only on the fixed class constants and the fixed bank.  Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) after taking the real part cannot increase distance from the real number \(\theta_0\), so (7) also bounds \(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0|\).

By \(\text{lem:empirical-transform-uniform-l2}\) and \(m_a\ge n/3\), for a uniform \(K_1<\infty\),
\[
 E_P[d_a^2+e_a^2]\le\frac{K_1}{n}. \tag{8}
\]
Markov's inequality and (8) give
\[
 P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)
 \le\frac{K_2}{n}. \tag{9}
\]
On the complement of the regular event, clipping gives the deterministic loss bound \((\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0)^2\le4C_{\theta}^2\).  Combining (7)--(9),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0)^2]
 &\le 2L_{\star}^2E_P[d_1^2+e_1^2]
   +4C_{\theta}^2P(\mathcal A_0^c\cup\mathcal A_1^c)\\
 &\le\frac{C}{n}. \tag{10}
 \end{aligned}
\]
All constants are uniform in \(P\) and \(n\).  The bank constants depend only on \((r,\delta,\psi_{\eta})\), while the other bounds use only the class constants displayed in the theorem.  Taking the supremum proves the upper risk bound.  Since the minimax infimum ranges over this estimator as one permissible sample map,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]. \tag{11}
\]

For the lower bound, invoke \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\), and let \(c_0,C_0\) be its constants.  Choose a fixed
\[
 0<h\le\min\{c_0,1,(8C_0)^{-1/2}\},
 \qquad
 \vartheta_-=-\frac{h}{2\sqrt n},
 \qquad
 \vartheta_+=\frac{h}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
Both parameter values lie in the submodel and have separation \(h/\sqrt n\).  The lemma gives
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_-}^{\otimes n}
 \|P_{n,\vartheta_+}^{\otimes n})\le\frac18. \tag{12}
\]
For completeness, (12) implies total variation at most \(1/4\).  Indeed, for \(A=\{dP_-/d\mu\ge dP_+/d\mu\}\), binary partitioning and nonnegativity of conditional relative entropy give
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_-\|P_+)
 \ge u\log\frac uv+(1-u)\log\frac{1-u}{1-v},
\]
where \(u=P_-(A)\), \(v=P_+(A)\), and \(u-v=\lVert P_--P_+\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  As a function of \(u\), the right-hand side has value and first derivative zero at \(u=v\), while its second derivative is \(1/\{u(1-u)\}\ge4\).  Therefore it is at least \(2(u-v)^2\), proving
\[
 \lVert P_--P_+\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_-\|P_+)/2}\le\frac14. \tag{13}
\]

For any estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), use the test \(A_{\widetilde\theta}=\{\widetilde\theta\ge0\}\).  On this event under \(P_-\), or on its complement under \(P_+\), the estimation error is at least \(h/(2\sqrt n)\).  Hence (13) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &E_{P_-}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_-)^2]
 +E_{P_+}[(\widetilde\theta-\vartheta_+)^2]\\
 &\quad\ge\frac{h^2}{4n}
 \{P_-(A_{\widetilde\theta})+P_+(A_{\widetilde\theta}^c)\}\\
 &\quad\ge\frac{h^2}{4n}
 \{1-\lVert P_--P_+\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \ge\frac{3h^2}{16n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the larger of the two risks is at least \(3h^2/(32n)\).  Taking the supremum over the class and then the infimum over estimators proves the lower bound with \(c=3h^2/32>0\).

The construction in \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) uses \(Y\), \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), and the once-for-all bank, but not \(\bar q_n\), \(\widehat q_n\), or the law of \(\eta\).  Finally, (10) and Markov's inequality imply
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|
 >\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}
 \right)\le\gamma.
\]
By the definition of \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}\), this is exactly the asserted generalized-quantile bound.  The class-inclusion disclaimer follows directly from the separate definitions of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).

Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).  By \(\text{def:ace-comparison-subclass}\), \(P\) satisfies every member property of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and also
\[
 \lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \lVert\bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
Since \(P_X\) is a probability measure and \(s\ge r+1>r\), Lyapunov's inequality, with its usual \(L^{\infty}\) interpretation, gives
\[
 \lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^r(P_X)}
 \le\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
and the identical argument gives
\[
 \lVert\bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^r(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]
All remaining member properties in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) are already properties of the broad non-Gaussian class.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
This is only a one-way inclusion for the explicitly restricted comparison subclass; neither definition supplies either of the broader relations disclaimed in the statement.

Suppose next that \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds and \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\).  Applying \(\text{lem:jms-ace-quantile-upper}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), and then restricting the supremum to the just-proved subclass, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)\\
 &\quad\le C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
 +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{31mm}
 +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
 \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}\Big],
\end{aligned}
\]
which is exactly \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).

It remains to justify \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\).  Fix \(u\in(0,\varepsilon_{1,n}]\), and enlarge only the outcome-code radius for the fixed experiment from zero to \(u\).  Every law satisfying the zero-radius restriction also satisfies the enlarged restriction.  Moreover,
\[
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},u,
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}
 =
 \max\!\left\{\varepsilon_{1,n},0,
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\right\}.
\]
Thus \(b_{2,n}\), and hence the exact eligibility predicate, is unchanged.  Applying the positive-radius result to the enlarged class bounds the zero-radius left-hand side by
\[
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[\varepsilon_{1,n}^ru+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
 +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
 \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}\Big].
\]
Letting \(u\downarrow0\) proves the displayed boundary formula.  Positivity of \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) is exactly what permits this monotone extension without changing the maximum in the eligibility condition.

Finally suppose \(n\ge2\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\).  The comparison subclass is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  If it is nonempty, \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)
 \le\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}};
\]
if it is empty, the uniform assertion is vacuous.  Along any asymptotic sequence on which
\[
 A_n:=\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
      +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
 \gg n^{-1/2},
\]
the fixed positive prefactors in \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\) give
\[
 B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\asymp A_n,
 \qquad
 n^{-1/2}=o(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}).
\]
Hence the spectral \(O(n^{-1/2})\) generalized-quantile guarantee is strictly smaller in order.  Only two upper guarantees have been compared; no risk lower bound for the ACE statistic follows.
statements.justification: The proposition isolates the exact subclass on which the published ACE comparison and its constants are licensed.
statements.gap: The broad direct-L1 spectral class has neither the treatment Ls condition nor the outcome-code condition required for the published ACE class.
statements.consumer: A referee can audit the one-way subclass inclusion, exact eligibility, constants, and zero-radius extension.

statements.statement:
Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) as external inputs to the two separate branches. Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the broad separated non-Gaussian branch satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}.
\]
This includes fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\); the witnessing statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\), as well as membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), imposes no restriction on and makes no use of \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Separately, every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection defined in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). Whenever that intersection is nonempty,
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) diagnoses an incompatibility internal to the simultaneous exact-PLM, bounded-\(Y\), and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian assumptions stated in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2. The positive lower-bound claim from that theorem is not relied upon here. No equality or inclusion between the two branches is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the deterministic code pair, clipped code pair, and nested radii in the statement.  Along any index satisfying \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) gives constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\) and of the class member, such that
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\frac Cn.
\]
Therefore \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}\) along every sequence of such indices.  Inspection of \(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\) shows that its membership restrictions involve \(\bar g_n\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\), but no supplied outcome code or outcome-code radius.  Inspection of \(\text{def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) likewise shows that the estimator is formed from \(Y\), \(T-\bar g_n(X)\), and the fixed contour bank, without \(\widehat q_n\), \(\bar q_n\), or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).  This proves every assertion about the non-Gaussian branch, including the fixed nonzero treatment-code regime.

For the separate Gaussian branch, \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) proves directly from the simultaneous restrictions in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) that every member has \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  If the class is nonempty, the same proposition and \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\) give
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
The proposition's proof uses the source theorem's simultaneous exact conditional-mean equation, bounded observed outcome, and nondegenerate conditional-Gaussian treatment residual: boundedness forces the conditional mean to be bounded, while a nonzero coefficient times the Gaussian residual has unbounded support.  Thus the diagnosed incompatibility is internal to those simultaneously stated assumptions.  The present result relies only on this direct proposition and does not rely on the positive lower-bound claim in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.  Finally, the two conclusions were proved on their separately defined classes, so no inclusion or equality between the branches has been used or established.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
Put \(a=\pi/2\).  A random variable with the stipulated mixture law can be represented as \(\eta=R+E\), where \(R\) is Rademacher, \(E\sim N(0,1)\), and \(R\) and \(E\) are independent.  Therefore
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]=e^{z^2/2}\cosh z,
\qquad
M(ia)=e^{-a^2/2}\cos a=0.
\]
The variable \(\eta\) is centered, \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), and
\[
E_P[\eta^4]
=E_P[(R+E)^4]
=E_P[R^4]+6E_P[R^2]E_P[E^2]+E_P[E^4]
=1+6+3=10.
\]
The fourth cumulant identity \(\kappa_4(U)=E[U^4]-3E[U^2]^2\) for a centered random variable now gives
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=10-3\cdot 2^2=-2.
\]

We next establish the denominator identity and its boundary modulus.  The characteristic function of \(\eta\) is
\[
\phi(t)=E_P[e^{it\eta}]=e^{-t^2/2}\cos t.
\]
For every deterministic \(d\in\mathbb R\), symmetry of \(\eta\) and differentiation under the expectation, justified by the Gaussian-mixture moments, imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{t(\eta+d)\}]
&=-\frac{d}{dt}E_P[\cos\{t(\eta+d)\}]\\
&=-\frac{d}{dt}\{\phi(t)\cos(td)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\phi(a)=0\) and \(\phi'(a)=-e^{-a^2/2}\), evaluation at \(t=a\) yields
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=e^{-a^2/2}\cos(ad).
\]
The independence condition \(\eta\perp X\), and hence independence of \(\eta\) and the \(X\)-measurable variable \(D_n\), permits conditioning on \(D_n\).  Since \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), this gives
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(aZ_n)]
=e^{-a^2/2}E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P[\cos(\pi D_n/2)].
\]

By construction \(\bar g_n\) takes values in \([-C_g,C_g]\), and the treatment-regression range assumption gives \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely.  Because \(s\ge1\) and \(P_X\) is a probability measure, the treatment-code radius and H\"older's inequality give
\[
E_P|D_n|\le \|D_n\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
The elementary inequality \(1-\cos u\le |u|\) therefore implies
\[
E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
\ge1-aE_P|D_n|
\ge1-\frac{\pi}{2}\frac1\pi
=\frac12.
\]
Thus the certified population denominator lower bound is
\[
c_0:=\frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}>0.
\]
This is the required overlap, relevance, and division condition; the estimator's cutoff ensures that it never divides by an empirical denominator smaller than \(c_0/2\).

It remains to prove the uniform risk bound.  Define
\[
W_i:=Z_{n,i}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
V_i:=\{Y_i-\theta_0(P)Z_{n,i}\}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\]
and write \(\bar W_n=\mathbb P_nW\) and \(\bar V_n=\mathbb P_nV\).  From the definitions of \(b_n\), \(Z_n\), and \(\xi\),
\[
Y-\theta_0(P)Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)D_n.
\]
Also, for every \(d\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=\operatorname{Im}\{e^{iad}\phi(a)\}=0.
\]
Consequently, treatment-noise independence gives
\[
E_P[b_n(X)\sin(aZ_n)]=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), outcome mean independence gives
\[
E_P[\xi\sin(aZ_n)]
=E_P\!\left[E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\sin(aZ_n)\right]=0.
\]
Hence \(E_P[V_i]=0\).

All second moments used below are uniform.  Indeed, with
\[
b_{\max}:=C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g,
\]
the support conditions give \(|b_n(X)|\le b_{\max}\).  The conditional sub-Gaussian assumption implies \(E_P[\xi^2]\le K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for an absolute constant \(K_{\xi}<\infty\) fixed by the convention for the \(\psi_2\)-norm.  Since \(|\sin u|\le1\),
\[
E_P[V_i^2]
\le2b_{\max}^2+2K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2
=:K_V.
\]
Likewise,
\[
E_P[W_i^2]
\le E_P[Z_n^2]
\le2E_P[\eta^2]+2E_P[D_n^2]
\le4+8C_g^2
=:K_W.
\]
These bounds also verify every integrability condition used in the conditioning, differentiation, and variance steps above.

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\{\bar W_n\ge c_0/2\}\), the event on which the sample ratio is used.  On \(\mathcal A_n\), projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\), and therefore
\[
|\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)|^2
\le \frac{\bar V_n^2}{\bar W_n^2}
\le \frac{4\bar V_n^2}{c_0^2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n^c\), both the clipped estimator and the target lie in \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\), so the squared loss is at most \(4C_{\theta}^2\).  If \(m_W=E_P[W_i]\), the denominator calculation gives \(m_W\ge c_0\); hence the independent and identically distributed sampling assumption and Chebyshev's inequality yield
\[
P(\mathcal A_n^c)
\le P\!\left(|\bar W_n-m_W|\ge\frac{c_0}{2}\right)
\le\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(W_i)}{nc_0^2}
\le\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}.
\]
The same sampling assumption and \(E_P[V_i]=0\) give
\[
E_P[\bar V_n^2]=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(V_i)}{n}\le\frac{K_V}{n}.
\]
Combining the regular and fallback events proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
&\le \frac{4K_V}{nc_0^2}
+4C_{\theta}^2\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}\\
&=\frac{4K_V+16C_{\theta}^2K_W}{c_0^2}\,\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The displayed constant depends only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), not on \(P\), \(n\), the supplied outcome code, or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).  This establishes the asserted uniform root-\(n\) mean-squared-error rate, including all support, positivity, overlap, and boundary conditions.

For \(n\ge2\), there is \(K<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) with \(|I_a|\ge1\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le \frac{K}{|I_a|}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m_a=|I_a|\) and let \(\mathbb P_a\) denote the empirical average on that half-sample.  The observations within \(I_a\) are independent under \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\).  Uniformly on \(|z|\le R_1\), the exponential series gives
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)
 =\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^p}{p!}(\mathbb P_a-P)Z_n^p
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)
 =\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^p}{p!}(\mathbb P_a-P)(YZ_n^p).
\]
For every square-integrable random variable \(W\), independence and centering give
\[
 \left\|(\mathbb P_a-P)W\right\|_{L^2(P^{\otimes m_a})}
 =m_a^{-1/2}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_P(W)}
 \le m_a^{-1/2}\lVert W\rVert_{L^2(P)}.
\]

Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the clipping bound \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\) imply that, for a class-uniform constant \(C_Z<\infty\),
\[
 \lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^p(P)}\le C_Z\sqrt p,
 \qquad p\ge2.
\]
Also \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\).  The boundedness of \(q_0\) and \(\theta_0\), the treatment sub-Gaussian bound, and the unconditional moment consequence of the conditional sub-Gaussian bound on \(\xi\) give
\[
 \lVert Y\rVert_{L^4(P)}\le C_Y
\]
uniformly over the class.  Consequently, for every integer \(p\ge1\),
\[
 \lVert Z_n^p\rVert_{L^2(P)}
 =\lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^{2p}(P)}^p
 \le(C\sqrt p)^p
\]
and, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \lVert YZ_n^p\rVert_{L^2(P)}
 \le\lVert Y\rVert_{L^4(P)}
     \lVert Z_n\rVert_{L^{4p}(P)}^p
 \le C(C\sqrt p)^p.
\]
The terms at \(p=0\) are bounded by the same conclusion after enlarging \(C\).

Minkowski's inequality now yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le m_a^{-1/2}\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^p(C\sqrt p)^p}{p!},\\
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le Cm_a^{-1/2}\sum_{p=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^p(C\sqrt p)^p}{p!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the \(p=0\) summand is interpreted as a separate finite constant.  For \(p\ge1\), the bound \(p!\ge(p/e)^p\) shows that the \(p\)-th summand is at most \((CR_1e/\sqrt p)^p\); hence the series is finite.  The same summable \(L^2\) majorant justifies the preceding termwise operations.  Squaring the two inequalities and enlarging the uniform constant proves
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le\frac K{m_a}.
\]

For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), the class's \(L^1(P_X)\) treatment-code restriction and clipping imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely and \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|
 \le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) throughout \(\{|z|\le R_1\}\), and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there with multiplicity.
statements.proof_tex:
Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) gives directly
\[
 E_P|D_n|
 =\lVert g_0-\bar g_n\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
The treatment regression and its clipped supplied code both take values in \([-C_g,C_g]\).  Therefore
\[
 |D_n|=|g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)|\le2C_g
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every \(w\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 e^w-1=w\int_0^1e^{tw}\,dt,
 \qquad
 |e^w-1|\le|w|e^{|w|}.
\]
Consequently, uniformly over \(|z|\le R_1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |H_n(z)-1|
 &\le E_P|e^{zD_n}-1|\\
 &\le |z|E_P[|D_n|e^{|z||D_n|}]\\
 &\le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0=\{4R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\}^{-1}\), this upper bound is at most \(1/4\), and hence
\[
 |H_n(z)|\ge1-|H_n(z)-1|\ge\frac34,
 \qquad |z|\le R_1.
\]
Thus \(H_n\) is zero-free throughout the disk.  By \(\text{lem:observable-factorization}\), \(F_n=MH_n\).  Multiplication by a nonvanishing analytic function neither creates a zero nor changes a zero's multiplicity, which proves the final assertion.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  The support restriction in \(\text{def:gaussian-class}\) gives
\[
 |Y|\le C_q
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{1}
\]
Because \(Y\) is bounded, all conditional expectations below exist.  Conditional Jensen's inequality gives
\[
 |q_0(X)|=|E_P[Y\mid X]|
 \le E_P[|Y|\mid X]\le C_q, \tag{2}
\]
and, on writing \(m(X,T)=E_P[Y\mid X,T]\),
\[
 |m(X,T)|\le E_P[|Y|\mid X,T]\le C_q
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{3}
\]
By the residual definitions,
\[
 Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta+\xi,
 \qquad
 \eta=T-g_0(X).
\]
Both \(q_0(X)\) and \(\eta\) are \(\sigma(X,T)\)-measurable.  The restriction \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) therefore implies
\[
 m(X,T)=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]

Suppose for contradiction that \(\theta_0(P)\ne0\).  Under the Gaussian-treatment restriction,
\[
 \theta_0(P)\eta
 \sim N(0,\theta_0(P)^2\sigma^2).
\]
The boundary condition \(\sigma>0\) makes this Gaussian nondegenerate.  Thus
\[
 A=\{\theta_0(P)\eta>2C_q\}
\]
has strictly positive probability.  On the intersection of \(A\) with the probability-one event on which (2)--(4) hold,
\[
 m(X,T)=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\eta
 \ge-C_q+\theta_0(P)\eta>C_q,
\]
contradicting (3).  Hence \(\theta_0(P)=0\).  Since \(n\) and \(P\) were arbitrary, this holds throughout \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).

Now suppose that the class is nonempty.  The statistic \(\widetilde\theta\equiv0\) is admissible in \(\text{def:minimax-risks}\).  For every class member,
\[
 (\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2=0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)=0.
\]
Both minimax criteria are nonnegative.  Taking the class supremum and then the infimum over all statistics proves
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 =\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}
 =0.
\]
Thus the zero statistic is minimax for both losses.  No overlap, positivity, rank, division, or inverse condition is used.  The finiteness of \(C_q\) supplies the support bound, \(\sigma>0\) supplies nondegenerate Gaussian support, and nonemptiness is needed only for the minimax display.

Specialize to \(k=4\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},
 \qquad
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and the direct condition \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Then
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
\]
\(t_a\) is the first positive characteristic zero, and \(E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=0\) for every real \(d\).  If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge A_a/2.
\]
Define
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is \(C<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that uniformly over these laws,
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for \(\Delta_a=2a^4\), the condition is \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\Delta_a^{1/4}/(2^{1/4}\pi)\), and the risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Independence of \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) gives
\[
 M_a(z)
 =E[e^{z\sqrt{1-a^2}G_{\circ}}]E[e^{zaS}]
 =\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az).
\]
Since the fourth derivative at zero of \(\log\cosh(az)\) is \(-2a^4\), the cumulant definition gives \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4\).  Its characteristic function is
\[
 \varphi_a(t)=M_a(it)
 =\exp\!\left(-\frac{1-a^2}{2}t^2\right)\cos(at).
\]
The exponential factor is positive, so the first positive zero is \(t_a=\pi/(2a)\), and for every real \(d\),
\[
 E[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]
 =\operatorname{Im}\{e^{it_ad}\varphi_a(t_a)\}=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \varphi_a'(t_a)
 =-a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}=-A_a.
\]
Differentiation under the expectation is justified because \(\eta_a\) has moments of every order.  Differentiating \(e^{itd}\varphi_a(t)\) and taking real parts at \(t_a\) yields
\[
 E[(\eta_a+d)\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}]=A_a\cos(t_ad).
\]
Since \(D_n\) is measurable in \(X\) and \(\eta_a\perp X\), conditioning on \(D_n\) gives
\[
 m_a:=E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]=A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)].
\]
The direct \(L^1(P_X)\) premise is exactly \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Hence \(1-\cos u\le|u|\) and \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) imply
\[
 E_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge1-t_aE_P|D_n|
 \ge\frac12,
\]
so \(m_a\ge A_a/2>0\).  This is the required overlap condition.

Put
\[
 W=Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 V=Y\sin(t_aZ_n),\qquad
 R=(Y-\theta_0Z_n)\sin(t_aZ_n).
\]
The residual identity is \(Y-\theta_0Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi\).  Conditional shift annihilation gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)\sin(t_aZ_n)]=0,
\]
and outcome mean independence gives
\[
 E_P[\xi\sin(t_aZ_n)]
 =E_P[\sin(t_aZ_n)E_P(\xi\mid X,T)]=0.
\]
Therefore \(E_P[R]=0\) and \(E_P[V]=\theta_0m_a\), establishing the population identifying moment separately from the sample ratio.

Clipping and the range condition give \(|D_n|\le2C_g\).  Since \(E[\eta_a^2]=1\) and \(\eta_a\perp D_n\),
\[
 E_P[W^2]\le E_P[Z_n^2]
 =1+E_P[D_n^2]\le1+4C_g^2=:K_W.
\]
Also \(|b_n(X)|\le C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g\).  The conditional sub-Gaussian premise implies \(E_P[\xi^2]\le c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for a universal convention-dependent \(c_{\psi}<\infty\).  Thus
\[
 E_P[R^2]
 \le2(C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g)^2+2c_{\psi}\psi_{\xi}^2=:K_R.
\]
Both constants are uniform in \(a,n,P\).

Write \(\overline W=\mathbb P_nW\), \(\overline V=\mathbb P_nV\), and \(\mathcal E=\{\overline W\ge A_a/4\}\).  Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) is a contraction and \(\theta_0\) belongs to that interval.  On \(\mathcal E\),
\[
 |\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|
 \le\frac{|\mathbb P_nR|}{\overline W}
 \le\frac4{A_a}|\mathbb P_nR|.
\]
Independence and \(E_P[R]=0\) yield
\[
 E_P[(\mathbb P_nR)^2]\le K_R/n.
\]
On \(\mathcal E^c\), the squared error is at most \(C_{\theta}^2\), while Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_a\ge A_a/2\) give
\[
 P(\mathcal E^c)
 \le P(|\overline W-m_a|\ge A_a/4)
 \le\frac{16K_W}{nA_a^2}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le\frac{16(K_R+C_{\theta}^2K_W)}{nA_a^2}.
\]
The independent deterministic bound \(|\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0|^2\le4C_{\theta}^2\), together with
\[
 A_a^{-2}=a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\},
\]
proves the first risk display.  Finally \(\Delta_a=2a^4\) gives
\[
 a=2^{-1/4}\Delta_a^{1/4},
 \qquad
 t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac12
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and
\[
 a^{-2}\exp\!\left\{\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right\}
 =\sqrt2e^{-\pi^2/4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left\{\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right\}.
\]
Absorbing the fixed prefactor into \(C\) completes the proof.  No supplied outcome code is used.

statements.statement:
The following two conclusions are valid, but they do not determine the full-class minimax phase diagram.

First, for each \(n\), let \(\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)\) be the class obtained from \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\) by replacing the fixed restriction \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta\) by \(\lvert\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)\rvert\ge\delta_n\), without changing any other restriction.  Define
\[
 \widetilde b_{2,n}
 =200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\delta_n
 \max\!\left\{
   \varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})
 \right\}^{-1}.
\]
Suppose \(\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), all logarithms and denominators in the following display are defined, and the exact local eligibility condition
\[
 r\le
 \min\!\left\{
   \frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
   -\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
   \frac{\widetilde b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2\widetilde b_{2,n})}
 \right\}
\]
holds.  Then the order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys the local oracle benchmark
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal C_n(\delta_n)}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)\\
 &\quad\le
 C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta_n^{-1}
 \Bigl[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\\
 &\hspace{42mm}
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
    \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
    (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
Denote the right-hand side by \(U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  If \(U_{\mathrm{DML},n}\) denotes a separately valid ordinary-DML upper bound under its own hypotheses, then \(\min\{U_{\mathrm{DML},n},U_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) is only an oracle upper envelope; this comparison neither asserts a minimax rate nor constructs a data-driven selector.

Second, specialize to \(k=4\), hence \(r=3\).  For \(0<a\le1\), let
\[
 \eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Its moment generating function, fourth cumulant, and first positive characteristic zero are
\[
 M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
 \qquad
 \kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4,
 \qquad
 t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a}.
\]
For every real \(d\),
\[
 E\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta_a+d)\}\right]=0.
\]
Consider any law satisfying \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), \(\eta=\eta_a\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(\lvert\theta_0(P)\rvert\le C_{\theta}\), \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\lVert\bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Put
\[
 A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\}.
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\), then
\[
 E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
 =A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
 \ge\frac{A_a}{2}.
\]
Writing \(\mathbb P_n\) for the empirical average, define the computable clipped ratio
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle
 \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}a^{-2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)
 \right\},
\]
where the supremum is over the just-displayed path laws.  Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4=\lvert\kappa_4(\eta_a)\rvert\), the condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le1/2\) is
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi},
\]
and the preceding risk is at most
\[
 C\min\!\left\{
  1,\frac{1}{n}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
  \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
This last display is a construction-specific upper bound with \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=O(\Delta_a^{1/4})\); it is not asserted to be sharp for the class specified only by a fourth-cumulant lower bound.
statements.justification: This is the strongest closed local-to-Gaussian result supported by the current proof spine: an exact published ACE specialization and an explicit pathwise spectral upper bound.
statements.gap: It supplies upper benchmarks but no full cumulant-only converse, quantitative contour-modulus theorem, adaptive switching theorem, or coverage result.
statements.consumer: A downstream analysis can use the displayed eligibility test and risk formula to compare finite-order and pathwise spectral procedures without mistaking either for the unresolved minimax frontier.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), the same externally supplied deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) is clipped and used in both branches; the pair may vary with \(n\) but is fixed before the independent inference sample is drawn.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment with the definitional residual \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\); the spectral branch imposes independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian noise, while the Gaussian comparator branch is exactly the known-variance bounded-outcome class of Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; spectral relevance is a positive winding number with a boundary modulus bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The deterministic radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) are nonincreasing, so the uncertainty balls are nested. The spectral estimator uses only \(\bar g_n\); the Gaussian comparison uses the same clipped pair and radii.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22) give the exact \(C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}[A_n+64V_n]\) generalized-quantile ACE upper bound over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). The proved inclusion \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) licenses comparison only on that narrower subclass; no broad-class inclusion is claimed.

Theorem 3.2 and equation (6) state the exact PLM with bounded observed \(Y\) and nondegenerate conditional Gaussian treatment noise and claim a positive generalized-quantile lower bound. Together with the theorem's stated conditional-mean restriction, those simultaneous source assumptions force \(\theta_0=0\); therefore the positive lower-bound claim is not relied upon here, and \(\text{prop:bounded-outcome-gaussian-degeneracy}\) records the incompatibility.
A second-order orthogonal PLM moment exists if and only if the treatment residual is non-Gaussian under their regularity conditions.
Transform conditions characterize completeness and incompleteness phenomena for location families.
An additive independent-error zero is inherited by an observable marginal characteristic function and can support a pointwise completeness test.
A bounded zero-free transform disk plus growth control yields a quantitative Gaussian approximation.
Linear independent-component methods estimate treatment effects under non-Gaussian source structure.

tldr: Complex zeros of the treatment-noise moment generating function yield exact shift-annihilating instruments. With \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), the established identities \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+M B_n\) give an observable contour formula for \(\theta_0\). The flagship theorem target proves, through compact-open closure, a finite uniformly conditioned contour bank and a measurable split-sample selector with uniform MSE \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), including fixed nonzero treatment-code error and arbitrary outcome-code error. The same deterministic code sequences and nested radii feed an exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bounded-outcome Gaussian branch, whose published generalized-quantile lower bound is converted explicitly to MSE. The resulting target is a Gaussian-versus-separated-non-Gaussian common-code dichotomy, with the local-to-Gaussian frontier left open.

project_justification.gap: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 gives a finite-order ACE quantile upper bound, subject to condition (21), that retains treatment--outcome and treatment-only nuisance terms. Its Theorem 3.2 establishes the Gaussian quantile barrier on a different bounded-outcome class. Classical location-family theory recognizes transform zeros but does not convert learned-residual zero geometry into a causal estimator with uniform risk.
project_justification.niche: Independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise creates a global null space for every location shift induced by treatment-code error. Small fixed residual contamination preserves this geometry, and observable contours avoid estimating the unknown noise law.
project_justification.fill: The project formalizes the exact annihilator and contour identities, proves zero localization and a finite uniformly conditioned contour bank, establishes selector measurability and uniform \(L^2\) empirical-process bounds, derives \(n^{-1}\) upper and lower MSE bounds, and states the Gaussian comparator on its exact published class with the quantile-to-MSE bridge shown.

related_work: \cite{Robinson1988} supplies the partially linear conditional-mean model. \cite{ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML} supplies orthogonal scores and sample splitting but ordinarily uses both nuisance regressions. \cite{MackeySyrgkanisZadik2018} establishes a finite-order non-Gaussian orthogonality frontier and informs the contrast with exact annihilation. \cite[Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22)]{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025} is retained as the precise ACE comparator, with transfer only through \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and with the attested \(r!16^r\) and \(64\) constants unchanged. Theorem 3.2 of that paper is not imported into the present simultaneous bounded-observed-outcome Gaussian intersection, because the latter forces \(\theta_0=0\). \cite{Mattner1992} is the narrow classical location-family completeness background: it motivates transform null spaces but does not supply the learned-residual contour estimator or its minimax theorem. \cite{HuShiu2022} informs observable zero inheritance, \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021} informs zero localization, \cite{NeweyRobins2018} informs independent-fold evaluation, and \cite{ChackoViceira2003} is a complex-moment GMM precedent. \cite{LeeMesters2024} informs the weak-non-Gaussian open question. \cite{ReizingerEtAl2025} is adjacent non-Gaussian treatment-effect work but does not subsume learned-residual contour adaptation.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact shift-annihilation, transform factorization, contour identity, nuisance-factor bound, and mixture algebra are established analytic reductions. The compact-open closure of the cumulant-separated MGF class, preservation of cumulant separation under that closure, uniform zero count and boundary modulus, measurable finite-bank selector, uniform \(L^2\) empirical-process bounds for \(e^{zZ_n}\) and \(Ye^{zZ_n}\), failure-event control, and common-code parametric lower-submodel membership remain proof obligations for the flagship theorem. No assumption substitutes for these obligations.
honest_scope: The proposal's headline \(C/n\) upper bound and matching \(c/n\) lower bound are theorem targets for D0, not verified results. The ACE comparison is restricted to indices satisfying the exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis condition (21), and \(s\ge r+1\) is used only to imply the required \(L^r(P_X)\) controls; it does not make the two base classes identical. The Gaussian MSE statement is only the explicit loss consequence of the published bounded-outcome quantile theorem. When \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=0\), the contour formula reduces to a known-residual location-family instrument; for the symmetric Gaussian mixture it reduces to the sine-score proposition. The shrinking-separation risk and coverage frontier remains open.
